groups.title: Next.js App Router rendering model
groups.question: You are building a blog page in the Next.js App Router that reads posts from the database, has a like button and loads slow comments. Explain how rendering works and where each part runs.

followUps.Server components versus client componen: What can a server component do that a client component cannot, and the reverse?
followUps.Static rendering, dynamic rendering, and: How does Suspense let the page show before the slow comments have loaded?

evidence.text: Server components run only on the server, so they can read databases and secrets directly.
Server components cannot use state, effects or browser APIs.
use client marks where code starts running in the browser for interactivity.

notEnough: Only saying one renders on the server and one in the browser.

misconceptions.text: Says client components are never rendered on the server.

evidence.text: Static routes are rendered at build time and cached.
Using things like cookies or search params makes a route dynamic, rendered per request.
Suspense lets the server send the rest of the page first and stream the slow part in when it is ready.

notEnough: Only saying Suspense shows a loading state.

groups.title: File-based routing and the layout system
groups.question: Your app has a dashboard section with a shared sidebar and pages that fetch data that changes every minute. Explain how the App Router's files fit together and how fetching and caching work.

followUps.How layout.tsx, page.tsx, and loading.ts: How do layout, page and loading files work together for a route?
followUps.Data fetching in server components: fetc: How would you make a server component's fetch refresh every 60 seconds?

evidence.text: layout.tsx wraps the page.tsx of that segment and its children.
Layouts stay mounted when navigating between child pages, so they keep their state.
loading.tsx is shown automatically as a fallback while the page loads.
fetch in server components accepts caching options.
no-store fetches fresh data on every request.
A revalidate time like 60 seconds serves cached data and refreshes it in the background after that time.

groups.title: Setting up and navigating a Next.js App Router project
groups.question: You are adding pages for individual posts at /posts/123 and documentation pages at any depth, plus navigation between them. Explain how dynamic routes and client-side navigation work.

followUps.Dynamic routes with [slug] and catch-all: How do [id] and [...slug] folders differ, and what does generateStaticParams do?
followUps.The Link component and useRouter for cli: Why use the Link component instead of a plain anchor tag?

evidence.text: A folder named with brackets like [id] matches one URL segment and passes it as a param.
A catch-all segment like [...slug] matches any number of segments.
generateStaticParams lists which dynamic pages to build ahead of time.

notEnough: Only saying brackets make dynamic routes.

evidence.text: Link navigates without a full page reload.
It prefetches the target route in the background so navigation feels instant.
useRouter from next/navigation lets code navigate programmatically, for example after a form submit.

notEnough: Only saying Link is for navigation.

groups.title: Metadata, error boundaries, and loading states
groups.question: Your post pages have no titles in search results, and a missing post shows a crash screen instead of a helpful message. Explain how you would set metadata and handle errors per route.

followUps.Generating SEO metadata with the Metadat: How would you give each post page its own title and preview image?
followUps.error.tsx and not-found.tsx for route-le: What do error.tsx and not-found.tsx handle, and why must error.tsx be a client component?

evidence.text: A page or layout exports a metadata object or a generateMetadata function.
generateMetadata can fetch the post on the server to build the title and description.
Open Graph fields set the preview shown when the link is shared.

notEnough: Only saying you set the title tag.

evidence.text: error.tsx catches errors in its route segment and shows a fallback with a way to retry.
It must be a client component because it uses a reset function to re-render the segment.
not-found.tsx is shown when code calls notFound, such as for a missing post.

notEnough: Only saying they show error pages.
